reason: The hypothesis cites no prior evidence, and its key premises about tungsten segregation behavior, boundary strengthening, and creep improvement in high-entropy alloys are specific claims requiring experimental support, which is absent.
premises: Tungsten atoms can be made to preferentially segregate to grain boundaries in a high-entropy alloy via controlled annealing.
Tungsten segregation at grain boundaries forms a layer or precipitates that strengthen the boundaries.
Strengthened grain boundaries reduce grain boundary sliding.
Reduced grain boundary sliding enhances creep resistance at elevated temperatures.
The effect is achievable in a conventionally cast, polycrystalline high-entropy alloy.
